## Context

CI LLM reviewers in standard, deep, and overlay tiers (running on the Python module + LiteLLM abstraction shipped by epic c6de-76e7-5e4b-4968) receive only the diff. Local `/dso:review` reviewers — running in Claude Code's harness with full tool access — make 20–40 grounded tool calls per review to verify call sites, deletion impact, cross-file consistency, and framework-guarantee defenses against the actual codebase. CI reviewers therefore produce lower-fidelity findings on the same diff: speculation about callers, missed cross-file regressions, and false-positive defenses that a quick `read_files` would refute.

This epic closes the CI ↔ local fidelity gap by adding an on-demand tool-use loop with batch tools (`read_files(paths[])`, `grep(patterns[], paths[])`) to standard / deep (3 specialists + arch synthesis) / overlay reviewers. Light tier stays diff-only because its job is fast feedback on low-risk changes and the loop overhead would erode that property.

Caching and exhaustion handling ship together with tool-use because they are load-bearing for one another: without prompt caching, the per-turn input-token cost across 15+ tool calls is prohibitive (the input prefix is re-sent every turn); without the soft-cap → second-nudge → fail-closed cascade, a misbehaving reviewer can loop indefinitely on a confused diff and either burn budget or hang the CI gate. Splitting them across separate epics would mean shipping tool-use with no cost ceiling first, then retrofitting cost controls — exactly the failure mode this epic is structured to prevent.

## Success Criteria

- Tool-use loop active for standard, deep (3 specialists + arch synthesis), and overlay reviewers; each can call `read_files(paths[])` and `grep(patterns[], paths[])` batch tools during their turn. Light tier dispatched without tool definitions and remains diff-only. Verified by tool-call logs in fixture-corpus runs evidencing standard / deep reviewers grounding findings in code reads (each such finding cites a `file:line` resolved by a recorded tool call), and light reviewers producing findings from the diff alone (no tool calls in the log). **Parallel-tool-result merge correctness**: a story 1 spike identifies whether any LiteLLM version correctly merges consecutive parallel tool results into the single user message Anthropic requires (LiteLLM discussion #18271, related issue #26529 on streaming translation); the spike artifact records the LiteLLM version tested and whether the merge gap is closed, giving future maintainers a clear upgrade path if LiteLLM resolves it upstream. If no version does, the tool-result assembly path in `dispatch.py` implements an application-layer merge before `litellm.completion` is called. Verified by a fixture replay test that emits two parallel `tool_use` blocks and asserts the Anthropic-bound request contains a single user message with both `tool_result` entries.
- `read_files` and `grep` tool implementations enforce a security boundary: repo-root jail (absolute paths and `..` parent traversal rejected); per-file size cap (configurable; default 256 KB); per-tool-result max output bytes (configurable; default 64 KB) with an explicit truncation marker appended when the cap is hit. Verified by unit tests covering absolute-path rejection, parent-traversal rejection, file-size-cap rejection, multi-pattern multi-path tool argument acceptance, and truncation-marker emission.
- Anthropic prompt caching active with two `cache_control` breakpoints (after the last tool definition; after the system+diff prefix). OpenAI prefix caching applies automatically. A cache-hit assertion (`usage.cache_creation_input_tokens > 0` on the first Anthropic call per review run) emits a warning to CI logs when cache creation does not occur, so silent invalidation regressions surface in build logs rather than only in billing data. Verified by unit test asserting `cache_control` placement and an integration test asserting `cache_creation_input_tokens > 0` against a fixture review.
- Soft-cap nudge cascade: a per-tier configurable soft cap (default ~15 turns) triggers a wrap-up nudge instructing the model to emit final `reviewer-findings` JSON. If the model continues tool-calling past a second cap threshold, a second harder nudge runs. If the model still does not emit final JSON, the review records as failed (fail-closed) via the existing `record-review.sh` integration. Verified by tests covering: nudge → final JSON path; second nudge → fail-closed recording; per-tier soft-cap override.
- Before / after fixture-corpus delta: post-tool-use CI runs surface a documented number of additional grounded findings (each citing a `file:line` resolved by a tool call) compared to the pre-tool-use baseline captured in story 1 of epic c6de-76e7-5e4b-4968. Comparison runs at epic close as a one-shot script and the delta is reported in the close artifact; per-fixture grounded-finding counts shift from zero (pre) to non-zero (post) on at least 60% of fixtures.
- Per-feature unit tests using `respx` / `httpx.MockTransport`-style provider mocks cover: tool-call dispatch (single + parallel `tool_use` blocks), soft-cap nudge state machine (each branch of the cascade), `cache_control` breakpoint placement under all four (tier × tools-present) combinations, jail enforcement, and output truncation. Integration tests exercise the tool-use loop end-to-end against both Anthropic and OpenAI providers with fixture reviews.

## Cross-Epic Interactions

- Resource: tool-mocking strategy in unit tests
  Interaction: e471-dda3 (Confluence integration / reference-library URL fetching) introduces curl-based fetching; this epic's tool-use loop's `read_files` is file-only (must NOT fetch URLs).
  Gate: document `read_files` semantics as filesystem-only; ensure the tool definition's description rules out URL fetching so the model does not attempt a URL argument.
- Resource: reviewer agent system prompts
  Interaction: 4911-c7ba (Reviewer rubric expansion) modifies reviewer prompts; this epic adds tool-availability instructions to reviewer prompts. Different regions of the prompt; both can proceed in parallel if the tool-use prompt section is added before 4911-c7ba's rubric expansion lands.
  Gate: parallel-safe; document tool availability in the rubric expansion so reviewers know which tools are available per tier.
- Resource: reviewer-findings.json finding shape
  Interaction: 4b8f-924d (Severity-only review schema) removes scores; this epic adds grounded findings that cite `file:line` evidence. Both modify the findings stream but at different layers (schema fields vs. finding-content shape).
  Gate: this epic's grounded-finding format must conform to whichever schema is current at merge time (post-4b8f-924d if it lands first; pre-4b8f-924d otherwise).

## Scenario Analysis

- read_files path traversal / unbounded reads outside repo (critical, runtime): unbounded paths or `..` traversal lets the model request `/etc/passwd`, `~/.aws/credentials`, or massive lockfiles, leaking sensitive content to provider logs. Mitigation: SC2 jail + size cap.
- Tool-use loop infinite ping-pong on malformed model output (high, runtime): generic error tool_results may cause retry loops that exhaust the soft cap on parser errors instead of grounding. Mitigation: SC4 nudge cascade plus structured tool_result errors that distinguish "your call was malformed" from "the file does not exist" so the model can self-correct.
- grep tool returns unbounded output and blows context window (high, runtime): broad patterns produce thousands of matches and can blow the context window mid-loop. Mitigation: SC2 max-bytes cap with truncation marker.
- Tool arg schema permits absolute paths and globs that escape repo (high, configuration): default `allowed_roots` exposure on misconfigured self-hosted runners. Mitigation: SC2 absolute-path rejection (no `allowed_roots` config — repo root is the only root).
- Prompt cache breakpoint invalidation on every run (medium, runtime): volatile fields (timestamps, run IDs, branch SHAs) in the cached prefix cause cache misses despite caching being "active." Mitigation: SC3 cache-hit assertion surfaces silent misses in CI logs immediately.
- Light-tier accidentally receives tool definitions (medium, configuration): a config refactor that defaults `tools=[...]` at the dispatcher and only opts out for light is one bug away from sending tools to light. Mitigation: SC1 explicit per-tier policy with opt-in, not opt-out, plus a unit test asserting light-tier dispatch carries no tool definitions.
- cache_control breakpoints misplaced when system prompt is empty or tools omitted (medium, configuration): unconditional placement produces a 400 from Anthropic on tier configurations that omit one or both blocks. Mitigation: SC3 four-combination unit test.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: c6de-76e7-5e4b-4968 (Python migration + LiteLLM provider abstraction — this epic operates on the merged dso_ci_review/ module).

## Research Findings

(Inherited from the parent brainstorm session; full citations live in c6de-76e7's spec.)

- LiteLLM tool-use parity across Anthropic + OpenAI is supported via OpenAI-format function-calling schema; parallel `tool_use` blocks pass through both providers.
- Anthropic cache prefix order is tools, system, then messages. `cache_control` on the last tool definition caches all tool definitions; up to 4 breakpoints. Two breakpoints (after tool defs; after system+diff) keep both cached across the multi-turn loop.
- OpenAI prefix caching is automatic for prompts ≥1024 tokens; no `cache_control` flag needed.
